title: SUST hall residents begin protest over provost conduct (Jan 13)
location: Begum Sirajunnesa Chowdhury Hall, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST), Sylhet
organizer: Female residential students of Begum Sirajunnesa Chowdhury Hall; no named organization is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance count is reported for the Jan13 hall gathering; the threshold of 50 is unverified.

start_date.summary: Both accounts place the beginning of the hall residents’ movement on the night of Jan13.

end_date.summary: The Jan14 action was temporarily halted and later protests resumed; neither source establishes a physical end for the Jan13 gathering.

location.summary: SUST Begum Sirajunnesa Chowdhury Hall; later actions moved to other campus sites.

scope.summary: A local hall-resident grievance; later campus-wide actions may belong to the same campaign but their physical relationship is unresolved.

organizer.summary: Residential women students; no named organizing body is identified.

demands.summary: Students demanded withdrawal/removal of the hall provost and assistant provost over alleged rude treatment and indifference to problems; no listed demand category is assigned pending policy/state-target review.

participants_original.summary: No count reported for this initial gathering.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No direct attendance estimate; the number of hall residents present is not specified.

protester_violence.summary: Not established for the Jan13 gathering.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is established for Jan13; later BCL and police actions are separate dates.

notes: This is the campaign’s initial hall protest, not a proxy for later numbers or later campus assemblies. Its demands concern hall administration; public-university authority and state-policy relevance remain open.
open_questions: Was the Jan13 gathering at least 50?
Does the provost grievance count as a demand on domestic state authority under the original coding rules?
When did this physical gathering end?

title: SUST students demonstrate after BCL attack; police disperse Jan16 gathering
location: Golchattor and ICT Building, SUST campus, Sylhet
organizer: SUST students; no named organization is reported.
participants_original: General students joined campus demonstrations; no attendance count is reported. A later police complaint named about 300 unnamed students in an alleged attack, which is not a crowd estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: The sources report wider student participation but no attendance count or other reliable lower bound; >=50 is pending.

start_date.summary: Sources date the larger student demonstrations and VC confinement to Jan16.

end_date.summary: Police dispersed protesters and released the confined VC; the specific gathering’s physical end after dispersal is not further described.

location.summary: Campus demonstrations at Golchattor; the VC was confined in the ICT Building.

scope.summary: Local SUST campus gathering; this is not conflated with Jan17’s fresh Golchattor sit-in.

organizer.summary: General students joined the protest; no separate named organizer is identified.

demands.summary: The report says general students supported prior demands and protested the Jan15 BCL attack; the exact demands pressed at the Jan16 assembly are not fully disaggregated.

participants_original.summary: General students joined; no turnout count. Police later filed a case naming about 300 unnamed students, not evidence of 300 attendees.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No meeting count; case against 300 unnamed students is a police allegation, not an attendance estimate.

protester_violence.summary: Police alleged student attack and injuries; protester violence against the state is not independently established and remains unknown.

state_response.summary: New Age reports police fired gunshots and used sound grenades during Jan16 dispersal; actual gunshots support shootings=yes, while sound grenades are separately recorded as dispersal evidence and are not treated as shots. Other accounts separately attribute allegations of student attacks; killings are not reported.

notes: Keep the Jan16 crowd, confrontation and police action separate from Jan17’s newly reported gathering. The police response is event-specific to Jan16, but size and exact state-directed demand remain unverified. The report distinguishes actual gunshots from sound grenades; the latter are not used as the shooting evidence.
open_questions: Was the Jan16 crowd at least 50?
Which explicit demands were pressed during this gathering, and were they directed at state policy?
Do source accounts distinguish the January15 BCL attack from the January16 VC confinement and dispersal?

title: SUST students gather at Golchattor demanding VC resignation (Jan17)
location: SUST Golchattor and nearby areas; a VC-residence sit-in was reported from 4:00pm the same day, with crowd continuity unresolved.
organizer: SUST students; no named organization is reported.
participants_original: Hundreds of students gathered at Golchattor and nearby areas; no exact count is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Daily Star says hundreds began gathering from about 8:00am, establishing at least 50 for the Jan17 Golchattor gathering. This does not establish the size of the preceding hall protest or the later residence sit-in.

start_date.summary: Daily Star dates the gathering to Jan17 and says students began assembling around 8:00am.

end_date.summary: No source establishes the physical ending of the Jan17 gathering or whether later actions were continuously occupied by the same people.

location.summary: Golchattor and nearby areas; a later same-day sit-in in front of the VC residence is reported separately without proof of same-crowd continuity.

scope.summary: Local SUST campus gathering; do not infer that it is a nationwide event from later solidarity actions.

organizer.summary: SUST students and student spokespeople; no named organization is identified as organizer.

demands.summary: Three demands: VC resignation for ordering police action, public apology, and accountability; student representative said they would petition President Abdul Hamid as university chancellor to dismiss the VC.

participants_original.summary: “Hundreds” gathered at Golchattor and nearby areas from about 8:00am; no exact count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound is encoded from qualitative “hundreds”.

participants_precision.summary: Qualitative estimate only; not converted to a point count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The contemporary report states hundreds gathered, clearly above the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific evidence establishes violence by protesters during the Jan17 gathering; Jan16 allegations are not assigned to this event.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response to the Jan17 gathering is established. Jan16 police dispersal and the earlier university closure are not attributed to this event. All seven dimensions remain unknown.

state_target.summary: The VC resignation demand was directed to the university; students explicitly proposed petitioning the President as SUST chancellor. The ministry’s laws page lists SUST under university laws and identifies the 1986 SUST Act, supporting the statutory domestic authority context. The body pages do not themselves use the exact label “public university”.

notes: The state-directed demand and threshold are supported. Jan17 Golchattor gathering and 4:00pm VC-residence sit-in may be the same group, but this is unverified. SUST is identified in a government ministry university-laws register under its 1986 Act; the explicit President-as-chancellor petition is the strongest state-authority evidence, rather than campus location.
open_questions: Did Golchattor participants move as a group to the 4:00pm residence sit-in?
When did the Jan17 physical assembly end?
Was the residence sit-in continuous overnight into Jan18?
Does the official university law documentation establish its public-status classification for this coding?

title: SUST sit-in and rallies outside VC residence with 24-person fast subset (Jan18–19)
location: In front of the SUST vice-chancellor’s residence, campus in Sylhet.
organizer: SUST students; no named organization is reported.
participants_original: Several hundred protesting students were present on Jan19. Twenty-four students began the fast unto death at about 3:00pm as a subset of the broader crowd.
threshold_50_evidence: New Age reports several hundred protesting students present while 24 began fasting; this establishes the gathering threshold, not 24 as total turnout.

start_date.summary: On its Jan19 account, New Age says the sit-in and rallies at the residence had continued without a break since Tuesday morning, Jan18.

end_date.summary: The report establishes continuous sitting/rallies through the start of the hunger strike on Jan19, but not the physical end after that day.

location.summary: In front of the SUST vice-chancellor’s residence.

scope.summary: Local SUST protest; possible physical continuity with Jan17 residence sit-in is not established.

organizer.summary: Protesting students and spokesperson Nusrat Arefin; no named organization is identified.

demands.summary: VC resignation and protest against police action; article says the VC was held responsible for ordering Jan16 police action.

participants_original.summary: Several hundred protesting students present; 24 began a fast unto death, a distinct subset.

participants_min.summary: No precise number or numerical lower bound encoded from “several hundred”.

participants_precision.summary: Qualitative estimate only; hunger-striker subset separately reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The contemporaneous report explicitly describes several hundred protesters present; 24 is only the fasting subset.

protester_violence.summary: Not established for the Jan18–19 sit-in; prior-day accusations are not applied.

state_response.summary: The Jan19 story describes later ministerial invitation to discuss on Jan22 but no meeting on Jan18–19; all seven response dimensions are unknown for this event.

state_target.summary: The demand concerns the SUST VC; a student said the President, also chancellor, would be petitioned to remove him. Government ministry university-laws register lists the SUST Act 1986.

notes: Attendance and state-directed VC demand are supported. Keep the 24 fasters as a subset, not total crowd. This residence gathering is documented continuously from Jan18 morning through Jan19; whether it is physically continuous with the Jan17 Golchattor/residence action remains unresolved.
open_questions: Did the Jan17 residence sit-in continue into Jan18 or end and restart?
What was the physical end of the sit-in/assembly after Jan19?
Did the hunger strike and broader sit-in maintain the same crowd or occupy separate physical boundaries?

title: SUST silent procession and residence sit-in amid ongoing VC protest (Jan22)
location: SUST campus main streets and in front of the vice-chancellor’s residence, Sylhet.
organizer: SUST students; no named organization is reported.
participants_original: Several hundred students held the silent procession; the 24 Jan19 fasters (with later hospital/return counts) were a subgroup of the ongoing campaign.
threshold_50_evidence: New Age reports several hundred participants in the Jan22 procession. This specific procession clears the threshold but does not establish a continuous crowd since Jan18.

start_date.summary: The Jan22 account describes a Saturday-evening programme and procession on Saturday, Jan22.

end_date.summary: The report says the procession was followed by a sit-in but does not report its physical end.

location.summary: Main campus streets and VC residence at SUST.

scope.summary: Local SUST campus procession and sit-in linked to the multi-day VC protest campaign.

organizer.summary: Protesting SUST students and spokesperson; no formal organization named.

demands.summary: VC resignation and protest at police action, according to article context and campaign demand.

participants_original.summary: Several hundred students in the silent procession; separate from the subset of hunger strikers.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound encoded from “several hundred”.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The article says several hundred students brought out the procession, supporting >=50.

protester_violence.summary: Not established for the Jan22 procession or sit-in.

state_response.summary: The education minister invited students to discuss the situation; students said they would discuss but keep the protest programme until their demand was met. The article reports no actual meeting; accommodation remains unknown.

state_target.summary: Demand for VC resignation remained active; earlier reporting identifies planned appeal to the President as chancellor and ministry lists the SUST Act.

notes: A discrete procession and follow-on sit-in are reported on Jan22. The source calls it the tenth consecutive day of the broader campaign, but this does not prove continuous physical attendance since Jan13 or Jan18. The hunger-striker count is not total procession turnout.
open_questions: Was the procession a distinct assembly from the ongoing residence occupation or did it consist of the same assembled students moving through campus?
Did the Jan22 sit-in continue uninterrupted from earlier residence gatherings?
What was the physical end of this protest action?

coding_history.reason: The source records an invitation and willingness to discuss, but no actual student-minister meeting or documented receipt/negotiation; invitation alone is insufficient evidence for yes.

title: Seven-college students protest exam postponement at Nilkhet and Dhaka University (Jan22)
location: Nilkhet crossing, moving to VC Square, University of Dhaka, Dhaka.
organizer: Degree students of seven government colleges affiliated with Dhaka University; no formal organizer is reported.
participants_original: No attendance count is provided in the accessible Bangla report. A separate Daily New Nation search result says “over 100”, but its body was unreadable and is not used to establish turnout.
threshold_50_evidence: Readable NewsBangla body identifies the participants and locations but gives no count. The >=50 threshold is not established; do not use the unverified search-result estimate.

start_date.summary: The article dates the demonstration to Saturday, Jan22 and says students arrived at Nilkhet at about 10:30am.

end_date.summary: Students moved from Nilkhet to DU VC Square around 11:05am; no physical end is reported.

location.summary: Roadblock at Nilkhet followed by procession/occupation at Dhaka University VC Square.

scope.summary: Local Dhaka assembly by seven government-college students; no other locations are reported.

organizer.summary: Degree students of seven government colleges affiliated with Dhaka University; no formal organizer named.

demands.summary: Students objected to abrupt exam postponement without notice and sought an explanation; deputy VC said closure was the government decision. Category mapping to social restrictions is provisional.

participants_original.summary: Seven-college students; no crowd estimate in the body.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Readable article does not quantify participants. The only “over 100” figure is in the search result for a second source whose body could not be retrieved, so threshold remains pending.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence reported; absence of reporting is not explicit evidence of no violence.

state_response.summary: A student reports a police officer warned that firing would clear the crowd and told students to move to the controller’s office; students then moved to DU. This is a reported crowd-dispersal warning, not evidence of actual shots. No arrest, beating, killing or actual shooting reported.

state_target.summary: Students asked the DU administration to explain the abrupt postponement. The deputy vice-chancellor said the closure of schools and colleges through Feb6 was a government decision. Whether the protest challenged that policy or sought administrative clarification remains unresolved.

notes: Attendance is unquantified in the article body. The state-policy link is explicit but the students’ immediate demand was an explanation from the university administration. A reported police warning and students’ move from Nilkhet to DU are preserved; there is no report of actual gunfire.
open_questions: Were at least 50 students physically present?
Did students demand a change to the government closure policy or only clarification from university administrators?
When did the occupation/protest at VC Square end?
